why_a_subnetwork.reason: route generation over the whole Greater Manchester network is impractical: 804,611 real road edges, and every observation that could constrain demand lies inside Manchester local authority.
why_a_subnetwork.authorised_by: the mission brief permits a reviewed Manchester-LA study subnetwork where whole-network route generation is impractical, provided its binding to the parent is preserved
why_a_subnetwork.measured_before_building: 285,782 parent edges were predicted to fall inside the local-authority box; the built subnetwork holds 285,794, a 12-edge difference

derivation.method: the accepted parent network was clipped, not re-derived from OpenStreetMap, so the subnetwork is provably a subset of the reviewed parent rather than a second independent build
derivation.boundary_source: the Manchester local-authority bounds derived from packaged generalised display geometry (network_scope.sub_area_bounds), the same bounds already used for the sub-area containment measurement

parent_binding.edge_id_check: all 285,794 study edge ids are present in the parent; none was renamed, so every accepted match binding remains valid against the subnetwork
parent_binding.note: --numerical-ids was retained for argument-vector consistency with the parent build. Verified rather than assumed: because the parent already carries numerical ids, the clip preserves them.

bound_edge_coverage.verdict: every edge the direction step bound a real observation to exists in the study subnetwork, so no observation is lost by working in it

boundaries_held.not_called_greater_manchester_wide: this is a Manchester local-authority study subnetwork. Calibration or comparison evidence produced in it is Manchester-LA evidence and must never be described as Greater Manchester-wide.
boundaries_held.no_demand_synthesised_outside_the_local_: Greater Manchester outside the local authority has no DfT observations and stays uncovered; a missing count never becomes a zero count.
boundaries_held.boundary_truncation_is_a_known_limitatio: routes generated in a clipped network necessarily start and end at the boundary rather than at true external origins. This is recorded as a limitation of the count-constrained candidate, which is not a claim about observed origin-destination travel in any case.

not_yet_done.tooling_verified_available: SUMO 1.27.1 with tools/routeSampler.py and tools/randomTrips.py; dfrouter deliberately unused because SUMO documentation warns it can produce implausible routes in highly meshed city networks

explicit_non_claims: a clipped subnetwork is geometry, not calibration, comparison, or validation
no demand artifact has been produced
no claim of routability is made here; connectivity was reviewed separately for the parent
MAN-09 remains planned and Gate D remains foundation_only
